fields.h1: Build a File Upload Form That Sorts Every File on Arrival
fields.hero_description: Build a file upload form that names every file by its submission and saves each response to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Happens to a File After Submit
fields.features_subheading: A file upload form collects documents and photos along with the answers. These six parts decide where each file ends up.
fields.feature_1:
Accepted types, checked on both ends

The form lists the file types it takes, and the browser steers people toward them. Browsers treat that list as a hint only, so the app checks each file's type again on arrival.
fields.feature_2:
Files renamed with the submission number

A phone photo called IMG_4471.jpg arrives as 3108-Moreno-receipt.jpg. You set the naming pattern in the prompt, and every file from one submission sorts next to the others.
fields.feature_3:
Each upload kept with its submission

Every submission saves as a row in a database you own, with its files listed beside the answers. There are no response caps, so a busy intake week never closes the form.
fields.feature_4:
Uploaded documents read into fields

The app can read an uploaded invoice, receipt, or form into fields such as the vendor, date, and total. Any field it reads with low confidence goes to a person to confirm.
fields.feature_5:
The right person hears about each file

Route each upload by an answer on the form: a resume to hiring, a signed lease to the office manager. The app sends an email, Slack, or in-app alert with the files listed.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

On paid plans, export the form's full code to your GitHub repository. A developer can then host it on your own servers and wire it into the other systems the business already runs.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Places the Files Go After Submit
fields.tab_content_1:
Each file in order 2207 arrives renamed

Penhale Print Works prints banners and asks for front and back artwork with every order. Joaquim Velloso uploads two files named final_v3.pdf and final_v3 (1).pdf. Prepress receives them as 2207-Velloso-front.pdf and 2207-Velloso-back.pdf, filed under order 2207.
fields.tab_content_2:
A leak photo goes to the on-call technician

Grace Lisowski rents unit 4B at Strand Hill Apartments. She picks Leak as the category and uploads 2 photos of the pipe under her sink. A request marked Leak skips the weekday queue: the app emails Hollis Iqbal, the on-call technician, with both photos and her unit number.
fields.tab_content_3:
Insurance that lapses in 21 days gets flagged

Quarrybank Builders keeps a current certificate of insurance for every subcontractor. When Rookwood Roofing uploads one, the app reads the policy end date. A policy that ends in 21 days breaks the 30-day rule: the certificate is flagged, and Tove Haverly, the project coordinator, gets a card asking for the renewal.
fields.tab_content_4:
Judges see entry 057, not who shot it

Cardew Camera Club's autumn contest takes up to 3 photos per member, and this year 38 members sent 104 photos. Each photo gets an entry number on arrival. The judging page shows only that number, and entry 057 is scored on the picture alone. Names return once scoring closes.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a File Upload Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a file upload form that names and routes every file, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List every file and who opens it
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Set the types each field accepts
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Pick a file name the team can sort
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Tie routing to an answer on the form
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each file you need, the person who opens it first, and what they do with it. A print shop's list reads: front artwork, back artwork, both to prepress. A file nobody acts on is a field to leave off.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give each upload field its own accepted types: photos as JPG or PNG, signed papers as PDF. Decide on a size limit per file too, and show both under the field label, where people read them before picking a file.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose a pattern built from the submission number, the sender's last name, and what the file is, such as 1045-Ito-lease.pdf. The number keeps two senders with the same last name apart in a long list.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Let one answer decide who hears about each upload. A deadline within 2 days might go to the account manager and anything later to the shared queue. Write each rule as one line before you write the prompt.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the file list, the accepted types, the naming pattern, and the routing rules into one prompt. Emergent builds the form, its database, and the alerts from it, and you change any part later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before sharing the link, try a wrong file type and a file over your size limit. Each one should be refused with a message that says what to send instead. Then submit a correct set and check the names and the alert.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Share the link where the files are
fields.howto_step_7_des: Expect photos of a leak or a receipt to come from a phone. Send the link by text, or print a QR code where the problem shows up. Open the form on a small screen first and finish one upload there yourself.

faq_plan.q: What is a file upload form?
faq_plan.a: A file upload form is a web form with at least one field that takes a file, such as a photo, a resume, or a signed document, alongside the typed answers. Each file stays tied to the submission it arrived with, and whoever reviews it can see who sent it and why.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a file upload form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: each upload field, the types it accepts, and what should happen to the file after submit. It builds the form and the database behind it. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What should a file upload form template include?
faq_plan.a: Start with the sender's name and email, then one upload field per file you need, each with a one-line note on what the file should show. Close with a confirmation screen that lists every file received by name. A file upload form template from a gallery gives you those fields; how files are named and who gets each one are still yours to add.

faq_plan.q: Can a free file upload form split uploads across several steps?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A multi step form can put each group of files on its own screen, such as identity documents on one and room photos on the next. People then see a short list at each step. Emergent is free to start, and that plan covers building and publishing a free file upload form like this one.

faq_plan.q: What file types should a file upload form accept?
faq_plan.a: Accept only the types the person opening the file can use, and set them field by field. A photo field might take JPG and PNG, while a signed agreement takes PDF alone. A field open to every type eventually receives a file nobody on the team can open.

faq_plan.q: How does a file upload form work in HTML?
faq_plan.a: It is a form element containing an input with type=file. MDN's guidance is to set the form's encoding to multipart/form-data whenever it contains an input with type=file. Code on your server then has to receive each file, check it, and save it with the rest of the submission.

faq_plan.q: Can I put a file upload form on a landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The form can sit in a section of the page or open from a button. For a contest or a casting call, an animated landing page can show last year's winning entries above the upload form. An app built with Emergent keeps every entry that arrives, with no response caps.

faq_plan.q: Can a file upload form take files from people who have no account?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the form is built as its own app: it can take files with no sign-in, or ask for one when you need to know exactly who sent each file. Other tools set their own rule. In Google Forms, responders need to sign in to a Google Account to answer a file upload question. Uploaded files are stored in a new folder in the form owner's Google Drive.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep files from a file upload form organized?
faq_plan.a: Give each file a name that starts with the submission number, and file it in one folder per client instead of one long list. If you run several file upload forms, add a short code for each form, such as LSE for leases, to the front of every name. An app built with Emergent can also copy each file to any storage tool with an API.

faq_plan.q: Can people upload photos from a phone camera to a file upload form?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the upload field accepts images. In HTML, the capture attribute specifies which camera to use for capturing an image or video on a phone. To get people to the form from a poster or a counter sign, a qr code landing page can open it in one scan.

domain_sources.claim: A form that contains a file input needs the multipart/form-data encoding
domain_sources.quote: multipart/form-data: Use this if the form contains <input> elements with type=file.

domain_sources.claim: The accept attribute only hints at file types and should be backed by server-side validation
domain_sources.quote: The accept attribute doesn't validate the types of the selected files; it provides hints for browsers to guide users towards selecting the correct file types. Because of this, you should make sure that the accept attribute is backed up by appropriate server-side validation.

domain_sources.claim: The capture attribute tells a file input which camera to use for an image or video
domain_sources.quote: The capture attribute value is a string that specifies which camera to use for capture of image or video data, if the accept attribute indicates that the input should be of one of those types.
